title: Credit Program Rules — The Residential Natural Gas Supply Sign-Up Credit
content:
**Rule 1 — earning (retired clause).** The former clause read: a gas plan whose sign-up credit amount is above 0.00 earns one sign-up credit once the agreement's completed billing cycles reach the plan's sign-up qualification count, posted on the bill of the next cycle. **This clause is no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied.

**Rule 2 — once per agreement.** The sign-up credit may be posted only once per agreement, as the agreement's ledger shows.

**Rule 3 — status.** Gas bill credits are posted only while the agreement is active or drop pending, as the agreement's status in the company's records shows.

**Rule 4 — forfeiture.** When the plan forfeits an unposted sign-up credit on a drop and the agreement left active status before qualifying, the credit is forfeited.

**Rule 5 — no sign-up credit for these events.** Plan changes, renewals and rollovers never earn a sign-up credit.

**Rule 6 — no other credit types.** Residential Natural Gas Supply agreements carry no referral credit and no dual-fuel credit; the dual-fuel benefit on a gas agreement is the service fee waiver of the gas supply billing rules.

**Rule 7 — credits and fees.** Credits are additive, each posted as its own line, and no credit offsets a termination fee.

### Judgement table

| Situation | Sign-up credit |
|---|---|
| A sign-up credit line already stands on the agreement | not posted again |
| Agreement status is closed | not posted (credits post only while active or drop pending) |
| Agreement left active status before qualifying, on a plan that forfeits on a drop | forfeited |
| The event is a plan change, a renewal or a rollover | never earns one |
| Customer asks for a referral or dual-fuel credit on the gas agreement | the gas agreement carries no such credit |

### Illustration (hypothetical)

An agreement owes an early termination fee and also holds a credit. Both stand as separate lines on the ledger; the credit does not offset the fee.
